git diff ba24972 -- idiomatic-elixir/ (working tree) changes "Read required keys with `map.key` or a pattern; keep `map[:key]` for optional keys" (three new paragraphs), rewrites "In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use", and adds one sentence to "Capture logs with `capture_log/2`, not a handler" in ex_unit.md. The nine rules graded for this case before are unchanged and are graded to the standard of evals/sweeps/2026-10-22-d/grades/library-client-skill.json. The two changed rules are newly indexed for this case and graded against their current text.

Read required keys: the sentence that decides the verdict for this case is "A pattern in a body that pulls one atom key or struct field out of a value the function already holds, with no literal and no guard, is dot access written long." The rule's text names maps and structs, so opts[:api_key] on the keyword list Keyword.validate!/2 returns (haiku-1 line 47, sonnet-2 line 107) is outside it; library-design.md's own example reads opts[:parts] the same way. First new bullet (re-match of a held value): 0 of 4 runs violated; 3 of 4 exercised it (haiku-1, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 read client fields with dot access in a body). haiku-2 did not exercise it: it reads the client's :req through a single-clause head pattern (line 54) and its bodies read no field of a value they hold. A run counts as exercising the bullet when a body reads an atom key or struct field out of a value the function holds; a case clause or pattern on a call's result is the kept form and does not count on its own.

In multi-clause functions: the sentence that decides the verdict is "A field no pattern or guard in the clause uses, bound in every clause of a function with three or more clauses, or bound in a head whose pattern `mix format` spreads over several lines, makes the reader scan every head to find what selects." Second new bullet (clutter in a function of three or more clauses): 0 of 4 runs violated; 4 of 4 exercised it (handle_response/1 has four, three, five and three clauses; haiku-1's Error.message/1 has three). Tuple elements bound beside a selecting tag (haiku-1 Error.message/1) are not counted as fields, as in the webhook-parser grades.

The bullet and the rule text disagree in two places. First, the bullet says no head's pattern spreads over several lines, while the rule text forbids that only when the head binds a field no pattern or guard uses: sonnet-1's handle_response/1 head at lines 140-150 spreads over eleven lines but binds only keys its guard reads (line 151), so it is clean under the rule and would be violated under the bullet's literal wording. Second, "a field ... bound in every clause" is read here as the same field in every clause. haiku-2's handle_response/1 binds body body-only in both Req.Response heads (lines 75, 80) and status in line 80, and escapes only because its third head is {:error, exception}. A reading where every head binds some body-only field, not necessarily the same one, changes nothing for the four check runs. I would align the bullet to the rule text and say in the rule whether "every clause" means the same field, since the previous sweep's results below turn on that.

Previous sweep re-read (evals/sweeps/2026-10-22-d/library-client, five baseline and five skill runs; grade files not edited). First bullet: 0 of 10 violated. The only body pattern on a held value is skill-haiku-1 to_forecast/1 line 120, %{"temperature_c" => temp_c, "condition" => condition, "wind_kph" => wind_kph} = body, which binds three string keys used together and is kept by the bullet. Second bullet under the rule text: 0 of 10 violated. Under the bullet's literal multi-line wording, 1 of 10: baseline-haiku-2 parse_forecast/1, a three-clause function whose second head spreads over lines 95-99 while binding only keys the guard reads (line 100). Under the every-head-binds-some-body-only-field reading, 3 of 10: baseline-opus-1 Error.message/1 (lines 204, 208, 212: status and message, message, body), skill-opus-1 Error.message/1 (lines 85, 89, 94, 98: details, status, status, details) and skill-sonnet-1 Error.message/1 (lines 149, 154, 158, 162: status, status, details, details); skill-sonnet-2's Error.message/1 escapes because line 178 binds only a guarded field.

Unchanged rules where this batch differs from the d sweep: haiku-1 breaks Group related parameters by listing its options under "## Options for `new/1`" in the @moduledoc (line 10) while new/1's @doc only points there (line 34). The earlier grades named the same placement as part of every such violation, though always alongside a missing Keyword.validate!/2; here the verdict rests on "document each one under `## Options` in `@doc`" alone. haiku-1 also breaks Use exception structs as error reasons: its @doc false Forecast.from_map/1 returns {:error, :invalid_body} (line 147), which forecast/3 wraps in a WeatherClient.Error (line 99) before any caller sees it. The 2026-10-22 baseline grade counted a private parser's atom reason the same way.

Unchanged rules outside the list, judged as in the d sweep: sonnet-1 breaks Match every expected shape, because its Error doc defines :api_error as a 4xx or 5xx status (line 7) while every non-200 status reaches it (lines 160 and 165, confirmed with a stub Req for 201 and 302). haiku-1, haiku-2 and sonnet-2 document their catch-alls to match.
